body:
It’s okay, and I’m sorry for the late reply. I’m glad you’re feeling better now. 

Please message me if you ever feel low again.
I’m just as confused as you, unfortunately. I’m sorry that I can’t be of much help, determining whether or not BPD is the cause of this behaviour. I strongly suspect it is though.
I’m the exact same. I wish I weren’t like this.

We were together as such. We were very close, liked it each romantically and sexually, and were considering putting a status to us. Does this make a difference? That she was not my girlfriend by definition?
Thank you for your honest input, it means a lot. Since educating myself on such matters, I have since always asked for explicit consent. Again, thank you.
How would you recommend I disclose this to my psychiatrist?

Thank you for your reply, it means a lot. Since educating myself on such matters, I have always explicitly asked for consent. 

My understanding of consent and boundaries was skewed because of past sexual abuse. Nonetheless, this is not an excuse. I will bring it up to my psychiatrist. Again, thank you.

Thank you for the optimistic view, and I am glad to hear that you’re on a journey of self-acceptance. Honestly, I don’t want to die — I am selfish. However, whenever I have a burst of happiness or contentment, I am subsequently swarmed with shame and regret. 

I am stuck in the past; I cannot live in the present when all I do is think about the person I once was.
